reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass continue holding in deeper sections of creek channel outer bends and structure depths of 10-16 feet. On warm sunny days over the past week, the surface temperatures on Millwood Lake felt like a late winter/early spring condition, and we noted a few male bass roaming shallow in backs of flats outside creek channels where spawning areas have been previously noted. This time of year, 3-5 degrees will make a big difference in the way bass respond and cruise in the backs of the creeks, and around spawning flats near stumps and where you have emergent vegetation. This time of year, cold, muddy water is the worst possible scenario for feeding bass.

I landed quite a few small spotted bass and 2 very nice largemouth bass. The bass hit the No. 7 Flicker Minnow and the crappie hit the No. The bass were coming off of the deeper side of the coves near rocky points.
I ended up cleaning three of the whites and the crappie for dinner Wednesday.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing ( 501-626-6899) reports that Peckerwood Lake has reopened for the season and anglers are catching crappie and catfish really well on poles and yo-yos.
Crappie can be caught on minnows and jigs (anglers are quiet about the colors they are using).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Donna Mulherin at Herman’s Landing ( 501-626-6899) reports anglers are catching crappie and catfish really well on poles and yo-yos.
Crappie can be caught on minnows and jigs (anglers are quiet about the colors they are using).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are either suspended at 10 feet on 25- to 35-feet flats adjacent to the main river channel or in brush from 5-20 feet deep.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has been up and down with the weather, but looks like we are ahead of the game.
While a lot of shad are high in the water column, out in the middle, in some areas bass left them as they went deep.
Crappie 101 Guide Service reports that most crappie are in the creeks now.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said anglers have been back to catching crappie in good numbers lately. Crappie are biting at about 2 feet, and the water is dropping fast now to about where it was before all the January rains, snow and ice came.
Anglers are also starting to pick up on some bass, and these also are good bass.
It’s mainly just crappie, they report.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some crappie are roaming around chewing while others are doing the same in pole timber or in brush piles — in all places they are suspended 4 feet down to 40 feet. Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points. Hybrid bass and whites bass are gorging like a lot of other species — when you find them, just about any metal bait you get in front of them will work, or swim bait, hair jig, inline spinners and some topwater, too, in 25-60 feet.
For bass fishing, it’s kind of spread out from deep to shallow. For the deeper fish, bass anglers are focusing on 15-20 foot of water and throwing a Damiki Rig, as well as an Alabama rig and a jerkbait…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie is somewhat slow and the fish have moved away from the shoreline out into deeper water. White bass have been caught but also in limited numbers. The slow results have been ongoing for two weeks, they said. Thursday, there were several people on the lake trying their luck in the more spring-like weather. The water is at a normal level and still muddy.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to react to the warming water, as some fish are showing up higher in the water column.
No reports on bass, catfish and bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: The month of March promises the beginning of the crappie spawn, which will add another quality game fish for the public to target.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass bite is slow. Reports have the bass scattered anywhere from 2 feet down to 20 feet. Kentucky bass also are slow. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are very good. Crappie are slow; try brush and structure 25-40 feet deep with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * The largemouth bass have been considering their move shallow. Two guys we saw up Little River had caught some decent largemouth on Chatterbaits and 1-Knocker Rat-L-Traps. The best feeding periods for largemouth bass have been from midday, continuing into midafternoon with increased sunlight in the 5-8 feet range. The oxbows along Little River from Mud Lake, all the way upriver to McGuire and Horseshoe Lake oxbows, have seen several male bass cruising in the flats. Those bass were chasing a quarter-ounce Rat-L-Trap Spin Trap, and a Bass Assassin 5-inch shad in the off-color water from 1-4 feet of depth near stumps. Chatterbaits in Spring Bream and Blue Ghost with a twin tail trailer picked…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“Several fish of different species are on shad in open water but the temperate bass are biting the best now. I am catching some crappie and bass ion main lake points in about 23 feet of water on brush just at and after sunset until dark.
“Three very nice largemouth and several white bass were feeding 35-40 deep and they really liked the white Tater Shad. The blue cat, whites and largemouth bass were all caught in the second area that I fished.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Most of the backwater fishing these days is for bass, with anglers targeting the shallow backwater areas off the main river.
No news from the crappie front on the river lately.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass measuring 11.02 and 12.6 pounds were taken on successive weekends at DeGray at the end of January and early February by area anglers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie is somewhat slow and the fish have moved away from the shoreline out into deeper water. White bass have been caught but also in limited numbers. The slow results have been ongoing for two weeks, they said. Thursday, there were several people on the lake trying their luck in the more springlike weather. The water is at a normal level and still muddy.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said the water level is high, the water temperature on Sunday was 48.4 degrees, and the crappie bite is good in the usual murky water. Anglers were catching crappie last week in minnows and jigs with skirts. Bass are in prespawn, she hears.
Make your plans now to hit that usual good spring crappie bite there.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Chicot fishing report
reports.text:
AGFC staff report quite a few angers are enjoying a strong midwinter crappie bite putting in from the Connerly Bayou out of access. AGFC biologists recently conducted an electrofishing survey of Lake Chicot in this area, showing several large crappie. Moderate crappie catch rates were noted in October and November in Ditch and Connerly bayous. During December, the biologists noted high crappie catch ra tes in Connerly Bayou and Lake Chicot and collected 1,318 crappie with trap nets. Of those crappie, 91 percent were legal size (greater than 10 inches). Most of the crappie sampled were in the 11-inch range, but some crappie sampled reached 14.75 inches.
Anglers also were catching good…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) says the crappie have been biting really with good size to the fish (about 2 pounds or more on several catches). Crappie are in the deeper parts and favor white/silver-white jigs and gray/silver-white jigs, as well as on minnows. Earlier in February, a crappie weighing 3.55 pounds was caught in a tournament on Erling, with a live minnow as bait.
Black bass have been active and biting.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie appear to be the main target now.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Chicot fishing report
reports.text:
AGFC staff report quite a few angers are enjoying a strong midwinter crappie bite putting in from the Connerly Bayou out of access. Anglers also were catching good numbers…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are doing well, but off and on.
“Bass are slow but should pick up with this warm weather.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Seth Boone, the superintendent at Lake Poinsett State Park, said Lake Poinsett is starting to do better with the crappie as the weather turns warmer. Bass are doing OK off the rocks with crankbaits and Zara Spooks in the wind.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
If someone were to go fishing, for bass fishing they suggest concentrating on the backwaters.
Crappie fisherman can look in the main river or backwaters for fish, according to reports they’ve heard with crappie holding there in about 15 feet of water. This is a good time for a black and chartreuse or white and chartreuse crappie jig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie were the exception as they were hitting fairly well. The crappie are in the top layer warming up.
“ Bass fishing should ramp up on suspended jerkbaits and Alabama rigs off main lake points adjacent to spawning areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Fishing guide Del Colvin at Bull Shoals Lake said Wednesday’s lake level was 655 feet msl, while the water temperature was 48 degrees. “ Bass fishing has slowed with the movement of baitfish.
Some bass left them as they went deep and some are holding above them at 30-60 feet.
Crappie 101 Guide Service says crappie are still pretty scattered in the creeks and main lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: The pond is 60 acres and has bass, crappie, bream and stocked rainbow trout.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass measuring 11.02 and 12.6 pounds were taken on successive weekends at DeGray by area anglers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some crappie are roaming around chewing, while others are doing the same in pole timber or in brush piles.
Black bass are good super shallow out to 50 feet in guts, main lake points or secondary points, on C-rigs, jerkbaits, football heads or crankbaits. Stay around the shad; the Wiggle Wart is working great. Also, a spoon or a Silverado-colored Rat-L-Trap is working. Walleye are doing what they usually do this time of year: following schools of bait around or disappearing. Spoons are working best around schools of bait. Catfish are hanging out on secondary points around and under baitfish or up rivers and creeks real shallow doing the same and gorging.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says fishing is kind of slow, but anglers are catching some crappie and other fish off the bank. For the crappie, some are using a pearl white crappie jig. But they report that overall there is too much water and the clarity is too muddy for much of a crappie bite nearer the bait shop.
Across the lake, however, they are using minnows on yo-yos and catching crappie as large as 14 inches in length.
They are expecting a better crappie bite in a couple of weeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie will be found deep in 25 feet of water and they are lethargic.
There were no reports on bream, bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
The bite for largemouth bass is slow. There are reports of bass around the edges of channels following baitfish. Look for bass around isolated structures looking for bream and shad around 18 feet of water. Kentucky bass are fair.
Crappie have slowed down, as they’re reported being found roaming in the channel but it’s been a slow bite. Crappie can be found on structures and brush anywhere from 20-35 feet in the channels.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are fair.
Crappie are still good and being caught on jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow to fair and still holding in deeper drops in the oxbows. Mike says they have not observed any females staging for the spawn yet, “but we anticipate that to begin in a few weeks.” Crappie are fair to good in 10-18 feet of depth away from river current on the main lake or in the oxbows. Crappie are best on jigs one day and minnows the next. White bass are still holding deep and have not shown up in large schools or numbers yet at Wilton Landing near Highway 71. Lots of river current present at Wilton from Cossatot River inflow. The AGFC and the Army Corps of Engineers have begun installing the additional security lighting at Yarborough Landing parking lot. Also, the…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Columbia fishing report
reports.text: Some really nice crappie are being caught there. In one particular report, a crappie angler brought in a couple of two pounds as part of his haul using a 1/16-ounce solid gray jig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) says the crappie have been biting really well and anglers have been catching a lot of good fish or 2 pounds or more. Crappie are still out in about 16 feet of water.
Crappie have been good there for the past month or so. Recently one angler caught a limit with eight of them being over 2 pounds each. In a crappie tournament held on Erling this past weekend, the Big Crappie caught weighed 3.55 pounds, hooked with a live minnow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fayetteville Boat Dock (479-444-3476) says anglers on boats out in the lake away from the shoreline have been catching both smallmouth bass and crappie of late. The smallmouth are taking to worms, while the crappie are favoring jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Anglers fishing in Saturday’s Anvil Jaw bass tournament caught plenty of largemouth bass and a few spotted bass during the rainy day earlier this month. Alabama rigs, jerkbaits and flat-sided crankbaits dominated most anglers’ front decks, with some anglers catching a few kicker bass on football jigs and Damiki rigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
One guy caught eight crappie (Wednesday), but it’s really been slow, the lake’s been up, and they haven’t wanted to get out, but it’s going down now.”
She hasn’t sold any bait for catfish or bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
A few anglers were out this week catching crappie — “nothing great, but they caught a few,” Ray said. Black bass are in 8-9 feet and biting on crankbaits and jigs, though not many of the bass were keepers.
During the coldest part of the weather recently, anglers were finding crappie via LiveScope on the bottom and not interested in taking a minnow — usually, that weather pattern produces a good crappie response but not this year, Ray said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Rock fishing report
reports.text: Late winter offers some of the best opportunities to land a trophy-class bass, trout, walleye or crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Anglers fishing in Saturday’s Anvil Jaw bass tournament caught plenty of largemouth bass and a few spotted bass during the rainy day. Alabama rigs, jerkbaits and flat-sided crankbaits dominated most anglers’ front decks, with some anglers catching a few kicker bass on football jigs and Damiki rigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
There are a lot of striper fishermen trolling around the Howard Cove area and catching a few small ones in the 5- to 8-pound range in open water on shad, and there are some black bass and white bass with them. “I have been mostly brush pile fishing for crappie and bass and the fishing has been poor during the day and fair in the evening. Some big crappie are being caught but not a lot. The bass fishing is getting better but not good yet.
“Three very nice largemouth and several white bass were feeding 35-40 deep and they really liked the white Tater Shad. The blue cat, whites and largemouth bass were all caught in the second area that I fished.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Andrews Bait Shop and More (479-272-4025) in Plainview hears from guides and anglers that crappie are doing very well now. Guide Jeff Larch, who operates River Valley Tours and takes groups out at Nimrod, went up in recent days to Dardanelle “and did very good on the crappie ,” they report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Andrews Bait Shop and More (479-272-4025) said Friday morning that the crappie are beginning to bite, and bite well. One of the guides going out from Andrews fished three days this week and on his teams the anglers were doing real well on the crappie.
Bass are slow and anglers are not catching many even up into the backwaters. Nobody is really catfishing now, and the bream anglers have not started bream fishing in number yet, though they were catching bream before the water took a big rise. Nimrod was 18 feet above normal pool level, but even with the latest rain it is dropping. The Corps of Engineers is “running it strong,” they report, and the water below the dam is at 314 feet msl. Above…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports that water temperature is in the mid-50s in Lake Langhofer to the low 60s in protected backwaters. Black bass can be caught with shallow-medium diving crankbaits, lipless crankbaits, spinnerbaits and bladed jigs along rocks and docks. Bass are not yet loading into typical early spwaning areas despite the abnormally warm temperatures.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Bass have been caught this week on Chatterbait (black/blue, a Z Man Jackhammer is a good one to throw now with more vibration to it than others), or flipping a black/blue jig as well as a square-bill crankbait. The bass are in the 5-foot range or shallower in these backwater areas. They have not heard much on the crappie fishing front, though, in the Little Rock Pool.
W hite bass, hybrid bass and striped bass will be catching all the knocked-around bait fish stunned in this water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Fishing has been good for crappie and mostly on structure of some sort in the 6- to 20-foot range.
We have been doing well catching spotted bass and largemouths throwing these baits for walleye, so that shows me bass are on the feed.
Crappie are rated fair to good. There are not a lot of crappie anglers out yet with the chill (35 degrees Friday) still in the air. The crappie are in a prespawn bite and found around brush and other cover. Many crappie anglers are using the LiveScope and searching them out and using a variety of baits, mostly jigs, artificials and minnows.
Black bass are still in a winter pattern and that bite is rate fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said crappie have been biting in the usual hot spots like Gold Creek. Crappie were reported at about 6 feet depth in Gold Creek, and at 6-8 feet depth around the Highway 89 bridge area. Bass anglers picking up topwater lures, Chatterbaits, buzzbaits, worms, shad-type flukes, creature baits and swimbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Crappie are back chewing pretty good since water has cleared back up.
Black bass are scattered all over, from shallow to deep.
Anglers have had success catching bass on a crawfish-colored Spro Rock Crawler and even throwing a spinnerbait in the stained water of the backs of creeks, too.
Crappie anglers haven’t provided much news from Greers Ferry Lake recently.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still biting but it’s difficult to catch them from the shoreline or dock.
“People are fishing 5-foot deep for crappie.”
(updated 2-23-2023) Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville says crappie are biting and are typical for the changing water of late because of the weather, so move around from shallow to deep water. Make sure you have the right color: Monkey Milk, black/chartreuse, Cajun Cricket, Kiwi, Mo-Glo, Silver, Blue Ice in jigs, or orange/white/diamond mist in Crappie Magnet.
Black bass are biting, but they’re slow. Also, the minnows and nightcrawlers that work for crappie may get a bass reaction. Watermelon red, red/blue/grape colors in…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: While there were no reports on bream yet, crappie, black bass, catfish and white bass were all reported caught in fair numbers. Minnows and jigs are working for crappie, and a few anglers reported getting bites. No baits were mentioned for black bass or catfish, either, but they were caught in fair numbers as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said b lack bass are still very good. Crappie are good on small jigs or minnows.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said, “ I know it’s still cold but the crappie and bass spawn is just around the corner. We are still catching crappie and other bass deep – 25-55 feet deep, but all the fish are going farther toward the river portions of the primary and secondary channels.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Over the past couple of weeks the largemouth and spotted bass have been randomly feeding along Little River and the oxbows with a few warmer days being best days to make a run upriver. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male bass were the most aggressive at midday into late afternoon recently, with those fish being found randomly near and close to deeper creek channels. The best bass reactions are random hits on Brazalo spinnerbaits in Spot Remover, Chatterbaits in white, and Rat-L-Traps in natural-colored crawfish browns and oranges or Toledo Gold and Red Chrome, and custom painted Bent Pole Little John Cranks in Rayburn Red finessed through the dead pad stems. The best water clarity and…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing starts to improve on both windblown banks on crankbaits back in the creeks and on main lake points near brush on grubs, and then another cold front comes through slowing the fishing. Crappie fishing is fair to poor on main lake brush piles on both jigs and live minnows on a slip float just at sundown to dark.
I got to land a couple of nice largemouth bass, a big 15-inch crappie, a handful of white bass and 4 hybrid stripers.
“With the rising water level, the largemouth bass bite will become really good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Fishing in the creeks feeding into the river can result in some nice bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports that water temperature is in the mid-50s in Lake Langhofer to the low 60s in protected backwaters. Black bass can be caught with shallow-medium diving crankbaits, lipless crankbaits, spinnerbaits and bladed jigs along rocks and docks. Bass are not yet loading into typical early spawning areas despite the abnormally warm temperatures.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are SLOW!
“For bass, what I gathered from the bass fishermen I spoke with, they are struggling as well with fish not responding to the warmer water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville says crappie are biting in spite of the various weather and water changes we’re seeing lately. Use jigs in Monkey Milk, black/chartreuse, Cajun Cricket, Kiwi, Mo-Glo, silver and Blue Ice, or throw a Crappie Magnet that is orange, white or Diamond Mist.
Bass are slow and anglers are not catching many even up into the backwaters. Nobody is really catfishing now, and the bream anglers have not started bream fishing in number yet, though they were catching bream before the water took a big rise. Nimrod was 18 feet above normal pool level, but even with the latest rain it is dropping. The Corps of Engineers is “running it…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: I caught a few nice crappie in the 13- to 14-inch range after sunset (Tuesday) evening on a grub and minnow, but not very many.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: The trout and smallmouth have been hitting well in the higher water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville says crappie are biting and are typical for the changing water of late because of the weather, so move around from shallow to deep water. Make sure you have the right color: Monkey Milk, black/chartreuse, Cajun Cricket, Kiwi, Mo-Glo, Silver, Blue Ice in jigs, or orange/white/diamond mist in Crappie Magnet.
Black bass are biting, but they’re slow. Also, the minnows and nightcrawlers that work for crappie may get a bass reaction. Watermelon red, red/blue/grape colors in artificials are good choices for bass here.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) reported that the crappie are moving to the shallows. Anglers are caching lots of nice-sized crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Lacey Williams at Lakeview Landing on Arkansas Highway 95 (501-252-1437) said that crappie anglers should look for the underwater timber about 5 feet deep and use minnows. No bream or bass reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Seth Boone, the superintendent at Lake Poinsett State Park, reported Lake Poinsett had crappie biting well on minnows and jigs. Bass are starting to bite on artificials off of the points. Crappie and bass are catch-and-release at Lake Poinsett.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are really starting to move up shallow.
Anglers have also been doing really well on the black bass, which are also coming up shallow in 3-4 feet of water. The yo-yos are working for crappie, too, and also on minnows.
“The main thing here is the crappie is moving up shallow.”

reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Last week was a pretty good week for people fishing for crappie, as it has been for the last two months or so.
“Spotted bass picked up last week on Alabama rigs and jerkbaits in the mid-lake area.
“Biggest change for me guiding was the crappie schooled up on mud flats in 25 feet of water. A lot of crappie were joining us for the fish fry with muddy tails, which shows me they are buried in the silt, which is common on these big temperature drops. You must learn what schooled-up crappie buried in the mud look like on your graph and then fish accordingly.
Crappie are good on minnows and jigs; work the brushpiles. Black bass are good, with crankbaits and worms working best.

reports.text:
The largemouth bass males continue to roam in 5-8 feet depth in creeks and bedding flats on warm afternoons, near vertical structure with the lake again falling. reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. Nothing reported on black bass, white bass or bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie reports were good. Nothing else reported in the regular Little Rock pool for bream, bass or catfish. Crappie in Pool 5 and below the dam are good. Best baits for crappie are the Super Jig Nos.
Crappie reports are good. The crappie are at 10 feet depth and are hitting jigs – blue/chartreuse and red/chartreuse are your winning combinations. Black bass are fair and are biting jerkbaits or a small jig.
However, anglers are having fair success with crappie or bass the past week. Bass are being found around rocky points and rock jetties and are hitting crankbaits and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair. Minnows and jigs are also on the crappie menu. Bass are fair. Alabama rigs and jerkbaits seem the ways to go for bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie “are biting pretty good at Lake Charles.” 6 crappie minnows and Kalin’s Grubs. Bass have been biting fair, too. Catfish are biting minnows, nightcrawlers and bait shrimp fished on the bottom, and you’re likely to catch a couple while crappie fishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: But across the board – bream, crappie, black bass and catfish – the reports were poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 18-30 feet eating at will on jigs and jigs tipped with minnows, around the warmest water you can find close to any timber. Black bass are eating in 15-60 feet of water with some largemouth being right on the bank; use spinnerbaits, crankbaits, or drag soft plastics in football head or C-rig.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Fishing was a little slow, with best results coming for crappie and bass anglers. Crappie were fair on minnows and jigs. Bass were reported as fair, but no baits were suggested.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is a little slow, with only bass being targeted. Bass reports were good, but no baits were revealed. Bream, crappie and catfish produced no reports the past week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: The Big Bass Shootout was held on Lake Maumelle Feb. Tracy Holder and Josh Ray, with 32.04 pounds, were third but had the biggest single bass, at 7.24 pounds. The Arkansas Top 12 High School Tournament finals also fished Sunday, with Aaron Joslin and KJ Terry of Bryant High School landing a 5.8-pound big bass and 13.82 total over five bass to win. On that note, Westrock notes that the largemouth bass bite is good. Kentucky bass fishing is poor. Crappie are good. Crappie are heading out of the deeper holes.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Until this spate of rough weather, crappie were biting well, though, on black/chartreuse jigs. Most of the crappie are being found in Porter Creek. Black bass were fair on spinnnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and the usual minnows and jigs will get their attention. Black bass action remains poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: 4 minnows and catching some good crappie. Bass have been biting minnows, spinnerbaits and jigs. Some good-sized bream have been biting the small crappie minnows of customers fishing for crappie. One customer set out to catch walleye on Winona and ended up with only a few good bass and one catfish,” she said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: The bite for bass improved over the past few days for largemouths during the midday hours in the oxbows. A 9-pound pound largemouth was caught over the past weekend. We continue to see good bass reactions with crankbaits, ¾-ounce slow-rolled War Eagle Spinnerbaits, and Rat-L-Traps in the creeks between 10-15 feet of depth. Bulky, fat tube jigs like 4-inch Gitzits, Brush Hogs, Bass Assassin Jingle Bugs or lizards, 10-12-inch bulky worms and Real Deal Custom Tackle Jigs continue taking a few chunky, largemouths in the creek channels from 10-15 feet deep on stumps, and on primary points with stumps from 6-10 feet deep. Green Pumpkin, Pumpkinseed/chartreuse, chartreuse pumpkin and blackberry…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been fairly good as of late, but still the frontal systems have affected their bite. I have landed some really nice slabs 30 feet down near the sunken brush piles. I typically use a 1/4 ounce spoon and jig it very slowly in and around the brush piles on the bottom. Live bait with a slip float or a minnow tipped to a small curly or paddle tail grub will work great.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Customers have been reporting catching some good smallmouth, Kentucky and largemouth bass as well as some good walleye. Crappie have been caught in the backwaters and around logs and brush in the deeper holes. 6 crappie minnows and Kalin’s Grubs have been doing the job.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie fishing has been slow. Bass are hitting minnows, small jigs and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bear Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Natalie Faughn, ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), reported that crappie are still biting well at Bear Creek and Storm Creek. No major reports on bass, although they do have some tournaments coming up and hope to have something to report on that next week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair and hanging off main lake points (usually on rocks that hold heat). Walleye and hybrids will mix in with the bass waiting for forage to come down the main channels. Crappie are really excellent right now over brushtops near creek and main channels in about 30-45 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been good on minnows or jigs. Bass reports have been good on spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text: Crappie fishing has been fairly good as of late, but still the frontal systems have affected their bite. I have landed some really nice slabs 30 feet down near the sunken brush piles. I typically use a ¼-ounce spoon and jig it very slowly in and around the brush piles on the bottom. Live bait with a slip float or a minnow tipped to a small curly or paddle tail grub will work great.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports that water temperatures are in the low to mid-40s. Fishing for black bass is very, very poor this time of year in this pool.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are beginning to invade brush piles when the surface temp is warmer and clear and will stack up even more as the water warms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: In those same areas, anglers are having fair success on crappie. Bass are fair. Try using spinnerbaits, crankbaits or jerkbaits for the black bass.

reports.text:
The fishing, particularly for crappie, stripers and white bass, has been good until the rains came, Tony reports.
However, anglers are having fair success with crappie or bass the past week. Bass are being found around rocky points and rock jetties and are hitting crankbaits and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Here again before the rain, a few hand-size crappie had been caught off of No. 6 crappie minnows off the dock and over off the bank across from the dock. Bass also were caught off of No. 6 crappie minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass were biting fair last week though they were very deep. Crappie last week were in the 10-15 range and biting well until all the rain and lake level rise.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are eating, and soon will be biting in 12-25 feet of water on jigs and jigs with minnows. Black bass are moving, too; try spinnerbaits, on windblown banks until water clears, then go back to C-rigs and football heads and small crankbaits as well as the blade.
Crappie have not really made their way out of the winter holding areas and can be quite difficult to stay with. The smallmouth bite has been best for bass fisherman on the lower end, while largemouth have been better in the shallower dirty water. “I’ll be updating reports over the coming weeks and it won’t be long until we are boating limits of crappie.

reports.text: Bream, crappie, black bass and catfish all rated poor by anglers this week. Before this week, crappie were biting well on minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: The best bets for these conditions while bass fishing are going to be brightly colored spinnerbaits, chatterbaits and crankbaits in chartreuse or orange. No crappie report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Lake Maumelle will be holding the 2019 Arkansas Big Bass Shootout on Saturday and Sunday with 70-100 boats expected on the lake. Largemouth bass reports are good for some, though other anglers say it is slow with the water temps dropping and water levels rising. Kentucky bass reports are poor. Crappie have slowed and are moving around; they are expected to be spawning in two weeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting well, though. Most of the crappie are being found in Porter Creek, but the bridge is already underwater. Crappie will bite minnows as well as black/chartreuse jigs. Black bass are fair on spinnnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie have been slow but are biting No. 6 crappie minnows fairly deep. Bass are being caught off of No. 12 bass minnows and pink and white spinnerbaits.

reports.text: Crappie are good and are biting minnows and jigs. Black bass are poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said a few crappie were caught off of No. 6 crappie minnows. Bass have been caught off of No. 12 bass minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Mike says the bite for bass improved over the past few days for largemouths, and is better during the midday hours in the oxbows. We continue to see good bass reactions with crankbaits, ¾-ounce slow-rolled War Eagle Spinnerbaits and Rat-L-Traps in the creeks between 10-15 feet of depth. Magnum 4-inch Gitzit Tubes with internal rattles are still drawing a few solid hits from solitary, 2-3-pound largemouth bass on stumps in outer creek channel bends, ditches, wash-outs, ridges and points in the oxbows.
Crappie continue improving in the oxbows, the clearest water you can find being the most activity areas, and are stacked up vertically over planted brush with jigs from 12-15 feet of depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: And quite a few smallmouth and Kentucky bass have been caught off of the brooders using a bronze 84A No. A few crappie, too, had been caught before it went up, some being caught on the brooder minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: A few bass have been caught off of brooder minnows. Crappie been deep with No. 6 crappie minnows and pink crappie minnows.

reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Recently, when the lake was normal, crappie were setting up about 20-25 feet on the bottom. White bass also were good two weeks ago, sitting on the bottom with the crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Columbia fishing report
reports.text: Sportsman’s One Stop in El Dorado (870-863-7248) reported that a few bass are being caught. No reports on crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Bass are good on topwater lures and on minnows. Nothing heard on crappie fishing.

reports.title: Lake Chicot fishing report
reports.text: Brian Whitson, park interpreter at Lake Chicot State Park, says crappie are biting on minnows and bright pink crappie jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are biting in 10-12 feet of water on red/chartreuse and black/chartreuse jigs. Anglers report a good bass bite, particularly around jetties.
Bream, crappie, bass, catfish and white bass all rated poor by anglers this week in the major areas of the Little Rock pool. Crappie are good and are being found in 15 feet depth.
Bass are fair on plastic worms, live worms and crankbaits. No bream were reported, and nothing was heard as far as crappie fishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie and catfish have been biting fair on No. Bass are hitting No.

reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were good the previous week, setting up about 20-25 feet on the bottom. White bass also were good a week ago, sitting on the bottom with the crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting well. The best catches are coming near the docks or around brush piles, and the crappie are in 10-15 feet depth. Bass are fair, but they are very deep in the lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are eating jigs and jigs with minnows in 25-30 feet of water around pole timber and brush piles. Black bass are eating Alabama rigs, jerkbaits, crankbaits and C-rigs, as well as football heads, hair jigs wacky rigs, etc. in 25-70 feet of water.
Crappie have not really made their way out of the winter holding areas and can be quite difficult to stay with. The smallmouth bite has been best for bass fisherman on the lower end, while largemouth have been better in the shallower dirty water. “I’ll be updating reports over the coming weeks and it won’t be long until we are boating limits of crappie.

reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Anglers only reported crappie catches, though the crappie catching was good. Nothing reported on bream, bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Anglers tried for crappie but reports were poor. Bass fishing also was poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is sluggish due to water temps and the increased pressure of fisherman practicing for upcoming tournaments. Bass are still, for the most part, deep in the 20-30 foot range, but when the sun comes out expect the fish to move up into depths of 10-15 feet, and feed near the main channel points over rip-rap and rocky areas (rocks hold heat). Crappie are smoking hot right now just over the tops of brush piles near the main channel and feeder creeks. Walleye and hybrids have been mixed in with bass-infested areas and are good attackers of vertical-fished white or chrome spoons.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good. Some reports are coming in that the largemouths are on the outer edge of the grass. Kentucky bass reports are poor. Some whites are being caught near brush piles stacked on the crappie in 20-30 feet of water. Crappie are good. Crappie are heading out of the deeper holes.

Crappie are fair on minnows and white/chartreuse jigs. Bass reports are fair.

reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair with minnows, spinnerbaits, jigs and some crankbaits. Crappie are “hibernating,” according to customers that usually catch a few on Norrell.

reports.text: Crappie are good, but they are favoring the deep water. Work the usual crappie baits around the bridges. Bass reports were poor.

reports.text: Crappie are fair. Bass are biting well.

reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said smallmouth and Kentucky bass have been biting well on No. Crappie have been biting pretty well in some deep holes and back waters on No.

reports.title: Bear Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Natalie Faughn, ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), reported that the crappie have been quite active both at Bear Creek and Storm Creek lakes this past week. Natalie said they have also had some bass fishermen out and about fishing with both jigs and crankbait in preparation of some fishing tournaments coming up at Bear Creek Lake – “they’re tight lipped about what worked and what didn’t,” she added.

reports.text: “I did not fish for bass this week, but they should be quite active.”

reports.text:
If you have followed my reports you know I love to fish for striped bass, hybrid bass and white bass, but if the bite is slow for these species you can switch up and go bass fishing, crappie fishing, walleye fishing or catfishing.”

reports.text: The river is looking great and the smallmouth bass and brown trout have been hitting.
